title: How NGINX Load Balances Traffic
hook: See how NGINX distributes traffic across application servers.

scenes.title: Sitting Between
scenes.narration: NGINX sits between users and application servers, receiving incoming requests and distributing them across backend instances. Users never interact directly with the backend servers when NGINX is used as a load balancer.

scenes.title: Round Robin
scenes.narration: By default, NGINX uses the Round Robin algorithm to spread traffic evenly between servers.

scenes.title: Least Connections
scenes.narration: The Least Connections load balancing method routes each request to the upstream server with the fewest active connections.

scenes.title: Upstream Directive
scenes.narration: The upstream directive in NGINX configuration is used to define a group of servers for load balancing.

scenes.title: Weight Parameter
scenes.narration: Load-balancing methods can be tuned using an optional weight parameter on the server directive to account for different processing capacities.

scenes.title: IP-Hash
scenes.narration: IP-hash load balancing uses a hash function to determine which server should be selected based on the client's IP address.
